Final Order Acquitted BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 01.

Succinctly stated the facts discernible from the present complaint are that the complainant was the owner of property bearing No. B-29/30/1 situated at Industrial Area of Jhilmil consisting of first and second floor.
It was alleged that the accused approached the complainant in the year 2004 to purchase the above said property for a consideration of rupees eight lakhs.
It was alleged that accused Shiv Kumar showed his inability to pay the entire amount of rupees eight lakhs in one go.
Hence, the accused paid an amount of rupees twenty thousand in cash and for balance amount of Rs. 7,80,000/-, he gave twenty six posted dated cheques in the sum of Rs.

It was further alleged that on assurance of the accused that the cheques would be honoured, the complainant executed a sale deed dated 24/3/2005 in respect of the above said property and handed over vacant and peaceful possession of the same.

It was further alleged that State vs Shiv Kumar on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11406502/

sentences.text: Further that accused cheated the complainant Madhu Aggarwal hence, an FIR against one Shiv Kumar (hereinafter, referred to as the accused) was registered under section 406/420 IPC.
COURT PROCEEDINGS 02.
After completion of the investigation, charge-sheet under sections 406/420 IPC was filed before the court against the accused.
The then Learned Magistrate took cognizance on 18.05.2009 and accused was summoned to face the trial.
On his appearance in the Court, copies of documents, relied upon by the prosecution were supplied to him as per norms.
Thereafter, vide order dated 01.09.2025, charge under sections 420 IPC was framed against the accused Shiv Kumar to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the matter was listed for PE.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 03.
The court heard final arguments on behalf of the both the parties on 1/12/2025.
Ld. Counsel for the accused submitted that the case against the accused is false and frivolous and has prayed that accused be acquitted of the offence charged.
Learned APP for the state submitted that accused be convicted of the offences under the above-mentioned sections as there is sufficient evidence on record to convict the accused.

This court has heard the submissions of Ld. APP for the State and Ld.
Counsel for the accused.
The court has also diligently gone through the charge-sheet, ISRA by ISRA ZAIDI ZAIDI 16:01:19 +0800 documents, evidence recorded and the entire material on record.
BRIEF REASONS FOR THE JUST DECISION OF THE CASE 04.

In the instant case, in order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution had to prove the following ingredients of the offence punishable u/s 420 IPC beyond reasonable doubt:
Section 420 IPC:
"Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine".
05.
Needless to mention, in criminal law, the burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.

State vs Shiv Kumar on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11406502/
2 06.
In the present case, complainant/Ms. Madhu Aggarwal was summoned through the concerned DCP.
The process was received back with a report that she had expired.
Thereafter, vide order dated 10.10.2025, she was dropped from the list of witnesses.
There is no other public witness, who was remained to be examined by the prosecution.
ISRA ZAIDI 16:01:25 07.
PE was closed as no fruitful purpose would have been served by examining the other witnesses.
Hence, continuation with the prosecution evidence would have been an exercise in futility.

Hence,
the opportunity to lead further prosecution evidence was closed.
Since there is nothing incriminating which is on record against the accused persons, the statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C. is dispensed with in the light of aforesaid legal position.

Reference may be made to a Division Bench judgment of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court passed in the case of Govind & Ors vs.
The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510 wherein it was held that:-
"...In cases where ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak or there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

entities.text:
Govind & Ors vs.
The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.
The trial should not be continued only for the purpose of formally completing the proceedings to pronounce the conclusion on a future date.........."
08. Since PW/complainant, who was a material witness could not be examined as she had expired even before her deposition and she was dropped from the list of witnesses.

Nothing could come out on the record to prove the incident or the necessary ingredients of the offences punishable under sections 420 IPC as there is no direct evidence to connect the accused persons with the crime.
09. The entire prosecution case hinged upon the statement of PW/complainant- star witness, who could not be examined.

Rest witnesses are formal in nature and the guilt of the accused cannot be established from their testimonies, in as much as, the alleged incident neither took place in their presence nor it is the case of the prosecution.

10. Therefore, keeping in view the overall conspectus of the case, this Court is of the considered view that the prosecution has miserably failed to discharge the Digitally signed by ISRA ISRA Date:
ZAIDI ZAIDI 16:01:31 2025.12.05 +0800 burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.
11.
It is an adage that law works on the wheels of evidence.
Every criminal trial is a journey of discovering and unfolding the truth.
But in the present case no sufficient evidence is there on record to warrant the conviction of the accused person.

In the case of Prem Singh Yadav Vs. CBI 178 (2011)
DLT 529 it was held that where it is possible to have both views one in favor of prosecution and one in favor of accused, the later one should prevail.

entities.text:
Prem Singh Yadav Vs. CBI 178 (2011)
DLT 529
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prosecution could not prove by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
In a criminal case the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The burden never shifts.
An accused enjoys the presumption of innocence.
There is no duty on an accused person to purge himself of guilt.

Where State vs Shiv Kumar on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11406502/
3 there is a lingering doubt, the accused person is given the benefit of the doubt.

12. For the reasons outlined above, this court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to discharge the heavy burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.
13. Consequently, accused namely Shiv Kumar is acquitted in the present case for the offence punishable under sections 420 IPC.
